clue.text: Underworld bosses moving East

indicators.note: moving says the letter for East shifts to another spot within the word for bosses

parts.note: heads are bosses, the people in charge
E is the compass abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: Company chiefs relocate to the eastern side of the business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' shifts the E of HEADS from second place to fourth, giving the underworld of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this is the realm of the dead, ruled by its god of the same name.

clue.text: London borough offering good prospects for schoolboys?

definitions.text: London borough offering good prospects for schoolboys?

parts.words: London borough offering good prospects for schoolboys?
parts.note: a famous public school sits on a hilltop in north-west London, giving its pupils fine views and fine futures

explanation.walkthrough: Harrow is a famous English public school on a hill in north-west London; 'prospects' means both views and career chances.
explanation.definitionFit: This district of the London Borough of Harrow is home to the public school of that name.

clue.text: Was first to set up newspaper in China

indicators.note: set up, in a down clue, means the word is written upwards, so reversed

parts.note: to have led is to have been first
FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone was the pioneer in launching a paper in China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country but means porcelain; 'set up' turns LED into DEL.
explanation.definitionFit: The blue-and-white glazed earthenware from the Dutch town is a kind of pottery or porcelain.

clue.text: Once a record defeat for the US

definitions.meaning: old gramophone records were made of a resin, before vinyl
American slang for a heavy beating or thrashing

explanation.definitionFit: 78 rpm discs were made of this resin; in American slang it also means to thrash an opponent.

clue.text: Gallery where one feels at home?

definitions.meaning: the famous art museum in St Petersburg bears this name
a recluse's retreat, where a solitary 'one' lives alone

explanation.definitionFit: A hermit's dwelling is a retreat for one person; the St Petersburg art museum shares the name.

clue.text: Familiar ingredient of Spanish omelette

indicators.note: ingredient of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A well-known component of a potato and egg dish from Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Something homely or close to one's heart is well known, as in 'home ground'.

clue.text: Carried by rifleman into bank, from what we hear

indicators.note: into says the soldier's word goes inside the word for bank

parts.note: to bank on is to rely on
a rifle held across the body at 'port arms' is said to be ported

explanation.surface: A soldier's gun was taken into a bank, so they say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port arms' is a drill order to hold the rifle diagonally across the body.
explanation.definitionFit: Something said to be so according to accounts is known by hearsay.

clue.text: As a deputy, detains crook

indicators.note: crook, read as an adjective meaning bent, says the letters are twisted

explanation.surface: A stand-in officer arrests a criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crook' looks like a criminal but is the anagram signal, as in Australian 'crook', meaning bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in place of someone else is what a substitute does.

clue.text: Outstanding score at golf resulting in handicap

definitions.meaning: three strokes under par on a hole, rarer than an eagle
a burden or encumbrance, after the bird in Coleridge's Ancient Mariner

explanation.definitionFit: Three under par on one hole is a rare golf feat; a burden is also named after Coleridge's seabird.

clue.text: The navy renowned at sea? Not always

indicators.note: at sea, meaning confused or adrift, says the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Is the famous fleet really out on the ocean? Only sometimes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' fits the navy but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something occasionally means doing it at intervals, not all the time.

clue.text: It charts country's rise and fall

definitions.text: It charts country's rise and fall

parts.words: It charts country's rise and fall
parts.note: reads like a history of a nation's fortunes, but it is a chart showing hills and valleys

explanation.definitionFit: A map showing the heights and depths of terrain charts land rising and falling.

clue.text: Book featured in The Times about old horse-soldier

indicators.note: featured in says the letter for book appears inside the other piece
about says the word for times is turned round

parts.note: eras are times, periods of history

explanation.surface: A book reviewed in the newspaper concerns a cavalryman of the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Times' looks like the newspaper, but only 'Times' works: ERAS, turned round by 'about', gives SARE, and 'featured in' puts B inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: By metonymy a cavalry soldier was named after his curved sword, as in 'a thousand sabres'.

clue.text: Ejected, knowing how to be a better pilot?

parts.note: someone ejected is put out
fly is informal for knowing or shrewd

explanation.surface: A pilot who has bailed out still knows how to fly better than the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: FLY in the sense 'knowing, artful' is informal British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: To fly faster or further than a rival aviator is to beat them in the air.

clue.text: Author's sound description of father

indicators.note: sound says the author's surname is said aloud, giving a word spelt differently

parts.note: J. B. Priestley was an English author and playwright

explanation.surface: A writer gives his own resonant account of his dad.
explanation.walkthrough: J. B. Priestley wrote An Inspector Calls; his name, spoken, matches an adjective for a cleric.
explanation.definitionFit: A Catholic father is a priest, so an adjective describing him suits a clergyman.

clue.text: Like colour of pitman, grey after shift

indicators.note: shift, read as a verb meaning move about, says the letters change places

explanation.surface: A miner turns grey after a long stint underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shift' looks like a miner's work period but signals the anagram; 'after' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective for colouring matter, as in skin pigment, describes something relating to colour.

clue.text: Fair target

definitions.meaning: impartial or unbiased, as in a fair judgment
an aim or goal to be achieved

explanation.definitionFit: An unbiased view is impartial; an aim or goal is also a noun with this spelling.

clue.text: Apologist? Only if that's right

parts.note: just means only, as in just one
taken as written
i.e. stands for id est, that is

explanation.surface: Someone says it would only be correct on one condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' stands for 'that is', i.e.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who defends or excuses a position makes a case in its favour, like a defender of a cause.

clue.text: Old mass included in musical performance in European cathedral

indicators.note: included in says the letters for old and mass go inside the other word

parts.note: a duo is a performance by two musicians
M is the physics symbol for mass

explanation.surface: An ancient Mass is part of a concert held in a cathedral on the Continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mass' looks religious beside 'cathedral' but just gives M.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian word for a city's principal church, used for cathedrals such as Florence's.

clue.text: Bit of culture

definitions.meaning: a small sample, as in a little piece to try
refinement and discernment in the arts

explanation.definitionFit: A small sampling of food is a little try; refined judgment in the arts is also called this.

clue.text: Ordeal that's shaken military leader in high office

indicators.note: this word means the letters it governs are mixed up, so they are rearranged into a new order
leader says only the first letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A general unsettled by a trial in a lofty post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shaken' rearranges ORDEAL into EARLDO; 'military leader' gives M.
explanation.definitionFit: The rank or title of a nobleman of the peerage is a lofty position.

clue.text: Rejected plan to introduce English ways into foreign islands

indicators.note: to introduce says the plan takes the other letters inside it
rejected means the word for plan is turned back

parts.note: an aim is a plan or intention
lanes are roads or ways

explanation.surface: A scheme to bring English customs to distant islands was turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rejected' turns the plan backwards to give MIA, and 'to introduce' says it takes the other letters inside. 'ways' looks like customs but means roads.
explanation.definitionFit: The island group in the south-west Pacific including Fiji and the Solomons is far from Britain.

clue.text: Happy with bill for bunch of flowers

parts.note: a bill is a beak, slang for the nose
gay in its older sense means happy or carefree

explanation.surface: Someone is glad to receive an invoice for a bouquet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bill' looks like an invoice but means a beak.
explanation.definitionFit: A small posy or bouquet is a small bunch of blooms.

clue.text: Settling elsewhere's an awful nightmare without husband

indicators.note: awful says the remaining letters are jumbled into a new order
without says the letter for husband is removed from the word

explanation.surface: Moving abroad is a terrible ordeal when one's spouse stays behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' drops the H from NIGHTMARE, leaving NIGTMARE, which 'awful' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone leaving their country to live in another is a person settling abroad.

clue.text: Man, perhaps, I fully extended

definitions.meaning: the Isle of Man is one example of a piece of land in the sea
I is the map abbreviation for this word, so writing it out in full gives the answer

explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man lies in the Irish Sea; 'Man' looks like a person.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is an example of land surrounded by sea, and I is its abbreviation on maps.

clue.text: One thing that's missing, unfortunately

parts.note: a means one
a lack is a want or absence of something

explanation.surface: An item has gone, sadly.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic exclamation of sorrow, like alas.

clue.text: Mix thoroughly in jug or can

definitions.meaning: to blend by moving a spoon round
both are slang terms for prison

explanation.walkthrough: 'jug' and 'can' look like containers but are slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Blending with a spoon is one sense; prison slang, as in 'doing time in', is the other.

clue.text: Surrealist recalled penning one long poem

indicators.note: penning says the reversed name encloses the letter for one
recalled, read as called back, turns the painter's name round

parts.note: Salvador Dali was the famous Surrealist painter
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A Surrealist painter remembered writing an epic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns DALI into ILAD, and 'penning' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's epic about the siege of Troy runs to over fifteen thousand lines of verse.

clue.text: Star signs to provide this

parts.note: 'Star signs' looks like the zodiac, but it is a celebrity signing a fan's book

explanation.definitionFit: A celebrity's signature given to a fan is the thing a famous person signs.

clue.text: Capital leader transformed old army soldiers

indicators.note: transformed says the letters of the preceding words are rearranged

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A veteran regiment of troops has been reformed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transformed' rearranges the letters of 'old army'; OR, for other ranks, is the usual crossword abbreviation for ordinary soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: The ceremonial head of the City of London holds this civic title.

clue.text: Territory in Canada that includes our state

indicators.note: includes says the word for that holds the other letters

parts.note: yon is an old word for that, as in yon hill
UK, the United Kingdom, is the state of a British setter

explanation.surface: A Canadian region that takes in our own country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'our state' is the British setter's country, the UK.
explanation.definitionFit: The far north-western region of Canada, famous for the Klondike gold rush, is a federal territory.
